body.statement: Fix a stratum of common-proxy rank \(q\). If the candidate menu contains a set \(F\) with \(r_q(E\cup F)=q(|V|-1)\), then adding the minimum-cost set \(F_*\) makes \(A_{P,x}\) attain rank \(q(|V|-1)\) for almost every attainable row collection. If this saturation holds in every stratum, then \(\ker(A_P)\subseteq\ker(R_0)\), so all target root contrasts \(\theta\) are generically identified for every compatible target latent mixture. Every feasible augmentation uses at least \(q(|V|-1)-r_q(E)\) new labeled trial edges in the fixed stratum, and equality holds whenever the menu contains an extension of a maximum union-independent set. If no such \(F\) exists, no choice of trials from the menu can remove the corresponding generic causal rank deficit.
body.justification: This is the novel causal design output: a certified trial addition is translated into attainable information rank, and an infeasible menu is declared causally futile.
body.gap: Weighted matroid augmentation is classical, but existing treatment-network design does not certify which additions exhaust the information attainable under a shared low-rank proxy kernel.
body.consumer: NETMOTION planners can distinguish a missing randomized comparison that completes the proxy-limited design from additions that leave the same causal ambiguity dimension.
